problems.title: A decimal linear equation
problems.question: Solve 0.9−0.2(1−3x)=4/5.
problems.idea: Distribute the negative coefficient.

problems.title: A constant after cancellations
problems.question: Evaluate (2x+y−1)²−4x(x+y−1)−y(y−2) at x=2/3,y=5/2.
problems.idea: Expand around y−1 to cancel all x terms.

problems.title: A ratio of differences of squares
problems.question: Evaluate (27²−63²)/(55²−35²).
problems.idea: Factor each difference.

problems.title: A required root makes a contradiction
problems.question: For which b does (b+2)(x−1)=2(x+b−2) have x=3 as a solution?
problems.idea: Substitute the required root before solving for b.

problems.title: Find a sum from two linear equations
problems.question: Find x+y if 8x−7y=31 and 4x+y=11.
problems.idea: Eliminate y using the second equation.

problems.title: A complement after a transversal angle
problems.question: Parallel lines a,b meet transversal c at A,B. One formed angle is 40° greater than another. K lies on a and KB⊥c. Find AKB.
problems.idea: Find the acute angle of the transversal first.
steps: u=70°. Triangle AKB is right at B and has angle A=70°.

problems.title: Factor using the root sum and product
problems.question: Factor x²−2x−35.
problems.idea: Find two integers with sum −2 and product −35.
steps: The factors are x−7 and x+5.

problems.title: Angle between tangents from an arc ratio
problems.question: A chord divides a circumference in ratio 7:11. Find the angle between the tangents at its endpoints.
problems.idea: The smaller arc determines the supplementary central angle.

problems.title: Compose a linear function twice
problems.question: Solve f(f(x))=9 if f(x)=2x−1.
problems.idea: Apply the function rule to its own output.

problems.title: Read a line from two intercepts
problems.question: Which equation describes the printed line through (0,3) and (2,0)?
problems.idea: Use slope and y-intercept.
steps: The constant term is 3, so y=−1.5x+3.

problems.title: Fractions of supplementary angles
problems.question: Two adjacent angles total 180°. Two fifths of one is 30° less than 80% of the other. Find the smaller angle.
problems.idea: Translate the comparison to a linear equation.

problems.title: Sum reciprocals of quadratic roots
problems.question: Find the sum of the reciprocals of the roots of (3x−1)²−25x²=0.
problems.idea: Factor the difference of squares.
steps: The roots are −1/2 and 1/8; both are nonzero.

problems.title: Half of two supplementary angles
problems.question: Bisectors of same-side interior angles between parallel lines make acute angles α,β with the lines. Their difference is 10°. Find the smaller.
problems.idea: The original same-side angles are supplementary.

problems.title: A division point compared with a midpoint
problems.question: A segment has length 2.8 m and is divided in ratio (2/3):(4/15). Find the distance from the division point to the midpoint.
problems.idea: Reduce the ratio before finding the pieces.
steps: The longer piece is (5/7)·2.8=2 m. The midpoint is 1.4 m from the same end.

problems.title: Count horizontal-line intersections with a piecewise graph
problems.question: For which b does f(x)=b have exactly one root, if f(x)=(x+3)/2 for x≤1 and f(x)=−2x+2 for x>1?
problems.idea: Count each branch’s output range separately.
formulas: First branch range=(−∞,2]; second branch range=(−∞,0).
steps: For b<0, each branch contributes one root, so there are two.
For 0≤b≤2 only the first branch contributes a root.
For b>2 there is no root.

problems.title: A side ratio fixes a midpoint ratio
problems.question: ABC is isosceles with AB=BC and its two different side lengths in ratio 2:1. M is midpoint of BC. Find (AB+BM):(AC+CM).
problems.idea: The equal legs must be the longer lengths; the alternative is a degenerate triangle.

problems.title: Six equal circles around one circle
problems.question: A circle of diameter 1 dm is touched externally by six equal circles, each also touching its two neighbours. Find their radii.
problems.idea: The six outer centres form a regular hexagon.
formulas: Adjacent centre distance=2r; distance to the central centre=R+r; a regular hexagon’s side equals its circumradius.
steps: The central radius is 0.5 dm=5 cm.

problems.title: A circumcentre on a triangle side
problems.question: The perpendicular bisectors of AB and BC meet on AC. What kind of triangle is ABC?
problems.idea: Their intersection is the circumcentre.
formulas: A chord through the circle centre is a diameter; an angle subtending a diameter is 90°.
steps: Thus AC is the circumcircle diameter and angle B is right.

problems.title: Distances from a parameter point to the axes
problems.question: A=(m−2,2m+3) is distance 5 from the x-axis. Which listed value can be its distance from the y-axis?
problems.idea: Distances to the axes are absolute coordinate values.
steps: m=1 or −4. The x-coordinates are −1 and −6.
The possible y-axis distances are 1 and 6; only 6 is listed.
problems.answer: Listed value 6; the full set of possible distances is {1,6}.

problems.title: Factor before substituting a complicated value
problems.question: Given a−2b=3 and a=7/2019, evaluate 2ab²−a²b+3ab.
problems.idea: Factor out ab.
steps: The relation a−2b=3 makes the bracket zero.
The numerical value of a is unnecessary.

problems.title: Complete an exponential square
problems.question: Which listed n makes 2⁸+2¹¹+2ⁿ a perfect square?
problems.idea: Recognize a square with a cross term.

problems.title: Work rates from two time combinations
problems.question: Two artisans finish a job together in 12 days. Two days of the first plus three days of the second complete 20%. How long for the first alone?
problems.idea: Let daily rates be u,v.
steps: Subtract twice the first equation to get v=1/5−1/6=1/30.

problems.title: An external secant angle
problems.question: A,B lie on a circle and D outside it. DA meets the circle at nearer E and farther A; DB at nearer C and farther B. ABC=90°,BCE=125°. Find ADB.
problems.idea: Use supplementary opposite angles of the cyclic quadrilateral.
steps: The remaining angle of triangle ADB is 180°−55°−90°.

problems.title: Coincident equations need both coefficient and constant ratios
problems.question: For which m does the system 5x−2y=12−mx, −x−y=3m−mx have infinitely many solutions?
problems.idea: Rewrite both equations with variables on the left.
steps: For coincidence, the first equation must be twice the second. Coefficients require m+5=2m−2, so m=7.
The constants instead require 12=6m, so m=2.
problems.note: At m=7 the equations are parallel and inconsistent, not identical. The correct choice is “none of the preceding”.

problems.title: Two reflections of a triangle vertex
problems.question: In ABC, A=52°,C=44°. Extend the median and altitude from B beyond AC by their own lengths to P,K. Find PCK.
problems.idea: P is the half-turn image of B about the midpoint of AC; K is its reflection across AC.
formulas: CP∥AB; CK is the reflected direction of CB.
steps: Taking AC as horizontal, both P,K lie on the other side of it from B.
CP makes angle 52° with CA, while CK makes 44° with CA on that same side.
